items.title: Phil Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 27, 2023
items.q: Lennie taught Bill Chase and myself at Berklee in 1955... And so Chase and I learned to lock in on each other. As a lead player I’d be playing lead trombone, he’d be playing lead trumpet beautifully

ctx.x: I was anticipating a train wreck actually.

It wasn’t. Haven’t you ever seen that video? You ought to check it out because I mean Chase and the five trumpets, three trombones you know, four saxophones up there and they — somebody had the smart idea, wouldn’t it be fun to match the early days of Woody Herman’s ’62 band when we played The Metropole in New York, the corner of Seventh and Broadway I think it was, something like that. 48th Street. It was the corner of 48th and Broadway. And every night, this is what put us on the map because they had a picture…
It was a very narrow stage, wasn’t it?
